Alright, let me recap where I am in the workflow. I have been iterating on the subagent delegation logic in the Glint CLI. The latest change was an edit to `src/core/agent.ts` that introduced tracking of already‑executed tool calls and a “nudged empty” flag to avoid infinite loops. After that edit, I triggered a rebuild of the CLI and a test run that uses the subagent to list the tools defined in `src/core/tools.ts`. 

The command I launched for that was:

```
cd /home/lane/GR/glint-cli && bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit &&
bun build src/index.tsx --compile --outfile dist/glint 2>&1 | tail -1 &&
cp dist/glint ~/.local/bin/glint &&
cd /tmp/glint-test &&
timeout 240 glint -p "Use the subagent tool to investigate which tool names are registered in /home/lane/GR/glint-cli/src/core/tools.ts, then report exactly what the subagent found." --yolo 2>&1 | tail -16
```

I launched it with `run_in_background: true`, so the system gave me a background task ID `b5dw1rrct` and told me that the output will be written to:

```
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lane-GR/e3d0c93f-5cf8-4067-9a49-657ba5c67c80/tasks/b5dw1rrct.output
```

Now I need to know whether that command succeeded, what the compilation messages were, and—most importantly—what the subagent actually reported about the tool list after my recent changes. The earlier background tasks (`be7wn3hwz` for the complex calc test and `bfdk5ryjj` for the initial subagent probe) have already completed and I have read their outputs. This new task is the only one still pending.

Given the overall goal—to verify that the subagent correctly enumerates the tools and that my salvage logic didn’t break anything—I must inspect the output of this build-and-test run before deciding on any further modifications. The most straightforward way is to read the file that the background process is writing to. Since the system provides a dedicated `Read` tool for exactly this purpose, I’ll invoke it with the path of the output file for task `b5dw1rrct`.

There’s no need to poll or loop here because the `Read` tool will return the current contents; if the process isn’t finished yet, the file may be empty or incomplete, but I can handle that in a later step. For now, the immediate next action is to fetch whatever has been written so far.

Thus, I will call the `Read` tool on the file:

`/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lane-GR/e3d0c93f-5cf8-4067-9a49-657ba5c67c80/tasks/b5dw1rrct.output`

to see the build logs, any compilation errors, and the subagent’s reported tool list.
